identification.summary: Storm-0538 is a Microsoft 'group in development' designation. Per the existing record it maps to FIN6 / SKELETON SPIDER, a financially motivated cybercrime group [S6]. MITRE describes FIN6 as a group that has stolen payment card data and sold it on underground marketplaces, aggressively targeting point-of-sale (PoS) systems in hospitality and retail [S7]. Mandiant (FireEye) observed it compromising retail and hospitality PoS systems from 2015 [S8]. Later reporting shows a shift to e-commerce skimming (Magecart-style), ransomware-linked intrusions and, by 2025, job-seeker phishing to deliver the more_eggs backdoor [S2][S1][S4].
identification.firstObserved: FireEye observed the group since 2015 compromising PoS systems of retail and hospitality organizations [S8]; FireEye first publicly identified it as FIN6 in April 2016 [S8].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Storm-0538 (group in development); the existing record lists FIN6 and SKELETON SPIDER (CrowdStrike) [S6]. Malpedia lists further synonyms including ATK88, Camouflage Tempest, G0037, GOLD FRANKLIN, ITG08, Magecart Group 6, TA4557, TAAL and White Giant [S6]. Caution: Proofpoint's TA4557 is described as historically overlapping with FIN6 and with tooling overlaps to Cobalt Group and Evilnum, not as identical [S5]; Malpedia's listing should be treated as an aggregator view. Storm-0538 is a different cluster from Storm-0539 (gift card fraud). I did not retrieve Microsoft's own page confirming the Storm-0538 to FIN6 mapping beyond the encyclopedia's imported mapping file [S6].

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor is identified in the sources gathered. Sources describe FIN6 as a financially motivated cybercrime group [S7][S1].
attribution.confidence: Mandiant stated in 2019 that FIN6 may have shifted to ransomware, or that some operators run ransomware intrusions independently of the card-data group, and that more research is needed; it noted that attribution is difficult because criminal relationships change often [S1]. Trend Micro tied the 2019 Volusion skimming campaign to FIN6 on the basis of code similarity with earlier activity [S3].
attribution.basis: Mandiant incident-response and Managed Defense observations [S1][S8]; Visa forensic investigations of e-commerce merchants [S2]; Trend Micro code comparison of skimmers [S3]; DomainTools infrastructure analysis (2025) [S4].

objectives: Financial gain: theft and resale of payment card data on underground marketplaces [S7], and later ransomware-related profit from access already held [S1].

targeting.notes: Retail and hospitality PoS targeting [S7][S8]; e-commerce merchants from September 2017 when PoS deployment was not possible [S2]; a Volusion-hosted set of 3,126 online shops in 2019 [S3]; an engineering-sector customer without payment data in 2019 [S1]; recruiters targeted via LinkedIn and Indeed in 2025 reporting [S4][S5]. The sources gathered do not give a country-level victim breakdown.

capabilities.summary: PoS malware: TRINITY (FrameworkPOS) [S2][S8]. E-commerce: injection of skimming code into merchant checkout pages [S2][S3]. 2019 ransomware-linked intrusion: compromise of an internet-facing system, RDP lateral movement with stolen credentials, Cobalt Strike and Metasploit, AdFind and 7-Zip for reconnaissance and staging, PsExec-based deployment of LockerGoga and Ryuk [S1]. 2025: fake job-seeker personas on LinkedIn and Indeed, AWS-hosted (CloudFront, EC2, S3) lure sites with traffic filtering and CAPTCHA, ZIP 'resume' delivering the more_eggs JavaScript backdoor [S4][S5]. more_eggs is attributed to a separate group, Golden Chickens (Venom Spider), of which FIN6 is a reported customer [S5].

campaigns.name: PoS intrusions in retail and hospitality
campaigns.summary: FireEye observed FIN6 compromising PoS systems of retail and hospitality organizations and using valid credentials to move within victim networks; stolen cards were sold on carder shops.

campaigns.name: Shift to card-not-present e-commerce theft
campaigns.summary: Visa reports forensic investigations of several merchants showed FIN6 targeting card-not-present data when it could not deploy PoS malware, placing skimming malware on checkout pages.

campaigns.name: Visa report on FIN6 e-commerce expansion
campaigns.summary: Visa published 'FIN6 Cybercrime Group Expands Threat to eCommerce Merchants'.

campaigns.name: Ransomware-linked intrusion (LockerGoga and Ryuk)
campaigns.summary: Mandiant described a FIN6 intrusion at an engineering customer using Cobalt Strike, Metasploit, AdFind and PsExec to deploy LockerGoga and Ryuk, and cautioned that the card-data group and ransomware operators might be separate.

campaigns.name: Volusion e-commerce platform skimming
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro reported Magecart-style skimming code in a library supplied by Volusion, active on 3,126 shops from 7 September 2019, and tied it to FIN6 by code similarity.

campaigns.name: Fake-resume lures hosted on AWS
campaigns.summary: DomainTools reported Skeleton Spider posing as job seekers on LinkedIn and Indeed, using AWS-hosted lure sites with evasion filtering to deliver more_eggs.

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated cybercrime group tracked as FIN6 / SKELETON SPIDER; Microsoft designation Storm-0538 [S6][S7].
diamond.capability: TRINITY PoS malware, web skimmers, Cobalt Strike, Metasploit, PsExec, LockerGoga/Ryuk deployment, more_eggs backdoor [S1][S2][S3][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: 2019: primary C2 176.126.85[.]207 plus other listed IPs and pastebin.com-hosted content [S1]. 2025: AWS-hosted lure sites (CloudFront, EC2, S3) and GoDaddy domain privacy [S4][S5].
diamond.victim: Retail, hospitality, e-commerce merchants, an engineering firm, and recruiters [S1][S2][S3][S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Profit-driven; no political objective is stated in the sources [S7].
diamond.technology: PoS terminals and payment-card data flows, e-commerce checkout JavaScript and platform-supplied libraries, internet-facing systems, RDP, Active Directory, and email/professional-networking platforms used by recruiters [S1][S2][S3][S4].

gaps: Microsoft's own published reporting on Storm-0538 was not found; the mapping to FIN6 and SKELETON SPIDER comes from the imported mapping file [S6].
Whether the 2019 ransomware activity was FIN6 itself or independent operators is unresolved per Mandiant [S1].
Alias boundaries (Camouflage Tempest, Magecart Group 6, TA4557, ITG08) rest on aggregators and secondary coverage; TA4557 is described as overlapping, not identical [S5][S6].

Primary documents not opened (fetch blocked or unreachable): MITRE ATT&CK G0037 page, the Visa PDF (summarized from search results only), Trend Micro and DomainTools full texts, the Dec 2024 DFIR Report case, and CrowdStrike SKELETON SPIDER reporting.
No victim list, geography, or law-enforcement action was verified; relevance to DoD or critical infrastructure targeting is not established.
Activity between 2020 and 2024 was not sourced.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain for this actor is payment and commerce infrastructure (PoS, merchant checkout pages), internet-facing systems, and recruiter-facing email and social platforms; for DoD this maps to exchange/commissary payment systems, MWR e-commerce, contractor networks and HR/recruiting functions [S1][S2][S4]. STEP 2: The actor is profit-driven and adapts quickly when one method is blocked, moving from PoS to e-commerce to ransomware-linked access [S1][S2]. STEP 3: Observed template is initial access via exposed system or social-engineered lure, then valid credentials and RDP, Cobalt Strike/Metasploit, AD discovery, and PsExec mass deployment [S1]; 2025 lures use job-seeker personas and AWS-hosted pages [S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued financial theft against commercial/retail and recruiter-facing targets. MDCOA is ransomware deployment against a DoD-adjacent contractor via an exposed system, causing mission disruption without state tasking [S1]. Candidate indicators: PsExec services mimicking msdtc ('mstdc'), AdFind and 7-Zip use on domain controllers, encoded PowerShell fetching from pastebin.com, unexpected JavaScript changes on checkout pages, ZIP 'resume' downloads from newly registered AWS-fronted domains [S1][S2][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track criminal-actor reporting separately from state-actor reporting, and note naming ambiguity (Storm-0538, FIN6, SKELETON SPIDER, TA4557) when correlating feeds [S5][S6]. (2) Authorities: criminal activity against DoD-adjacent commercial entities typically falls to law enforcement and DIB reporting channels rather than military cyber authorities; confirm the applicable authority before any action. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize hardening of internet-facing systems, RDP, and domain admin credential hygiene, and test restoration given ransomware-linked tradecraft [S1]; protect recruiting and HR staff from unsolicited resume lures [S4]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3/DIB partners and payment-sector contacts; treat vendor attributions as vendor assessments.
